title: Get fast proof of Intent source browsing and pinned links

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage — SEED-413#speed-intent-source-browsing-and-detours at c60b8fbed9b528809ab57aeab45a9a320542ce00

Verdict: Caught.

Promise: "Canonical and plan links use the inspected revision while external, unsafe, and invalid targets keep their distinct results." Probed path: an unsafe-scheme target (javascript:) must stay "unusable" with its reason, not become a snapshot link.

Fault (caller's suggestion validated and used): dashboard/src/sourceLink.ts line 123, resolveSourceLink: `if (scheme !== undefined) {` changed to `if (scheme !== undefined && false) {`, so every non-http(s) scheme falls through to repository-path resolution. Fixtures and assertions untouched.

Independent wrong-behavior witness (scratch node script importing production sourceLink.ts, outside the maintained tests): with the fault, resolveSourceLink("javascript:document.title='canonical-ran'", …) returned {kind:"snapshot", url:"https://github.com/acme/widgets/blob/abc1234def/.planning/javascript%3Adocument.title%3D'canonical-ran'"}; before the fault and after restoration it returned {kind:"unusable", reason:"Links that use “javascript:” are not opened from here."}. An ordinary snapshot link ("seeds/SEED-1.md#a") resolved identically in both states.

Maintained checks examined: dashboard/frontend-tests/navigation/source-link-rules.spec.ts and dashboard/frontend-tests/navigation/source-links.spec.ts (Vitest, mounted-chromium). e2e/navigation/source-navigation.spec.ts was not run: it belongs to the E2E group, not the focused frontend command, and the two frontend checks already caught the fault.

Command (scratch worktree, Node 24.21.0 per .node-version, after npm ci): `env -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR npm run --silent test:dashboard:frontend -- dashboard/frontend-tests/navigation/source-link-rules.spec.ts dashboard/frontend-tests/navigation/source-links.spec.ts --workers=2`, with OPEN_DOUGH_DASHBOARD_FRONTEND_PROOF_RECORD set to a fresh file each run.

Runs:
- Baseline: exit 0, 7/7 passed (proof record selectedCount 7, phase completed), including the two refusal cases.
- Faulted: exit 1, 2 failed, 5 passed. Catching assertions:
  1. source-link-rules.spec.ts:89:32, in "unsafe, traversing and incomplete targets are refused with their reason": `expect(resolved(recorded)).toEqual({ kind: "unusable", recorded, reason })` for the javascript: entry. Received kind "snapshot" with a URL at the inspected revision, which matches the witness.
  2. source-links.spec.ts:109:19, in "refused targets are readable text with their reason and no link": `expect(shown).toContain("Not offered as a link. Links that use “javascript:” are not opened from here.")`. The rendered WorkSourceLinks showed "Canonical record javascript:…File in this snapshot, at revision 9b1d4e6." instead. Its earlier toBeVisible on the traversal reason passed.
  The other 5 cases (canonical/plan snapshot links, external links, path decoding) still passed, so the failure was limited to the faulted path.
- Restored: the trap-based `git checkout -- dashboard/src/sourceLink.ts` ran. git status --short matched the pre-probe state (empty) and git diff was empty. The witness again returned "unusable". The same command exited 0 with 7/7 passed.
Cleanup: scratch worktree removed with `git worktree remove` and no longer listed. The execution checkout was not edited.

Claim bound: the catch covers the javascript: scheme in resolveSourceLink and its rendering in WorkSourceLinks. Traversal (../) refusal was not faulted separately. The same rules case lists "../../elsewhere/secret.md#top" and asserts on it, but this probe does not establish that.

Next proof action: none needed for this promise path. An optional separate probe could fault the traversal branch in repositoryPath.
Prior disposition: none matched. This probe causes no repair decision.

Costs:
- Test runtime: measured by the Vitest-reported Duration. Baseline 1.25 s, faulted 1.24 s, restored 1.07 s, about 3.6 s total. Wall clock for each npm invocation was about 2 s.
- Human effort: unavailable. No human took part during the probe, and there is no separate measure.
- Agent effort: unavailable. No separately supported token or time measure is available to this agent.

- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 67581 ms (measured), from 1795390633000 to 1795390700581 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

Wrap-up disposition: checked revision c60b8fbed9b528809ab57aeab45a9a320542ce00; verdict Caught; no follow-up.
